proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Open-ended Question 6. Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\). For every sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\), determine the epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit, in the weak topology, of the rescaled design-profile risks \(J^{4/3}\{\mathsf R_J-1/(2J)\}\) specified by the second-order pair-orbit selection handle \(\mathcal L_{(s_J)}\), and use its exact contact conditions to characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\). At \(\rho=1/2\) and finite \(\kappa=\lim_J\kappa_J\), prove or refute a matching lower expansion for the candidate upper-bound functional
\[
 \mu\longmapsto
 \mathcal A(\mu)+\kappa\left(2\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
 \qquad \mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},
\]
where \(\mathcal A\) is to be derived from the unrestricted Airy/local pair-orbit experiment. Treat \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) as the distinct one-sided, recentered, and tangent regimes specified in the handle. A complete answer must prove uniform lower and recovery expansions and must recover the proposed contact points by exact finite minimizers. The displayed hard-budget term is presently only upper-bound evidence; finite-grid calculations do not establish the asserted limit or exact-minimizer recovery.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original question leaves the smaller-order scale and limiting variational problem unspecified. The revised question isolates the critical scale, distinguishes all four asymptotic regimes, and asks only for the matching lower expansion and exact-minimizer contact theorem that remain unproved; it expressly demotes the available hard-budget formula to upper-bound evidence.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal L_{(s_J)}\) denote the following second-order selection problem. Put
\[
 \Delta_J=s_J-\frac J2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_J=\frac{\Delta_J}{J^{2/3}},
 \qquad
 \overline m_J(q)=\int_{\Delta_2}m(x)\,d\mu_q(x),
\]
and define the finite design-profile risk
\[
 \mathsf r^{\mathrm{prof}}_{J,s_J}(q)
 =\min_{\eta\in[-1,1]^{\mathcal N_J\times\mathcal O_J}}
   \max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s_J}}\mathcal R_h(q,\eta).
\]
On \(\mathcal P(\Delta_2)\), equipped with the weak topology, extend the grid profile by
\[
 \mathsf R_J(\mu)=
 \begin{cases}
 \mathsf r^{\mathrm{prof}}_{J,s_J}(q),&\mu=\mu_q\text{ for some }q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J),\\
 +\infty,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \Gamma_J(\mu)=J^{4/3}\left\{\mathsf R_J(\mu)-\frac1{2J}\right\}.
\]
The second-order pair-orbit selection problem is to derive, from the ten-type schedule experiment and the kernel \(K\), an unrestricted Airy/local-experiment functional \(\mathcal A\), and then to prove a matching liminf inequality, recovery bounds, convergence of minima, and exact-minimizer compactness for \(\Gamma_J\). At the critical boundary \(s_J/J\to1/2\) with \(\kappa_J\to\kappa\in\mathbb R\), the candidate upper-bound functional is
\[
 \Gamma^{\mathrm{up}}_\kappa(\mu)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \mathcal A(\mu)+\kappa\left(2\displaystyle\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
     &\mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},\\
 +\infty,&\mu\notin\mathcal F_{1/2}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The hard-budget term in this display is upper-bound evidence only until a uniform matching lower expansion is proved. If \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\), the residual problem must first restrict to the subface \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\). If \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), use the recentered functional
\[
 \widetilde\Gamma_J(\mu)
 =J^{4/3}\left\{\mathsf R_J(\mu)-\frac1{2J}-\frac{\Delta_J}{J^2}\right\}
\]
and analyze the subface \(\int m\,d\mu=1\). The regime \(\rho>1/2\) is a separate tangent problem on \(\mathcal F_\rho\), including transverse deviations of the finite-grid measures, and is not identified with the critical \(\kappa=+\infty\) problem. Only after the required lower and upper expansions are established may the contact sets of these limiting problems be compared with \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\); exact-minimizer recovery is an output to prove, not part of the definition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old handle neither defined the finite profile functional nor fixed the critical scaling, and it improperly placed exact-minimizer recovery inside a construction. The corrected handle defines the residual epi-limit problem, records the candidate hard-budget upper term, and separates finite, one-sided infinite, and fixed-supercritical regimes without asserting the missing theorem.

proposed.statement:
Open-ended Question 6. Put \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\). For every sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\), determine the epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit, in the weak topology, of the rescaled design-profile risks \(J^{4/3}\{\mathsf R_J-1/(2J)\}\) specified by the second-order pair-orbit selection handle \(\mathcal L_{(s_J)}\), and use its exact contact conditions to characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\). At \(\rho=1/2\) and finite \(\kappa=\lim_J\kappa_J\), prove or refute a matching lower expansion for the candidate upper-bound functional
\[
 \mu\longmapsto
 \mathcal A(\mu)+\kappa\left(2\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
 \qquad \mu\in\mathcal F_{1/2},
\]
where \(\mathcal A\) is to be derived from the unrestricted Airy/local pair-orbit experiment. Treat \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) as the distinct one-sided, recentered, and tangent regimes specified in the handle. A complete answer must prove uniform lower and recovery expansions and must recover the proposed contact points by exact finite minimizers. The displayed hard-budget term is presently only upper-bound evidence; finite-grid calculations do not establish the asserted limit or exact-minimizer recovery.
proposed.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face; the corrected question identifies the \(J^{2/3}\) critical budget scale on which that selection can first interact with the unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) correction.
proposed.gap: The unrestricted Airy expansion does not supply a measure-valued pair-orbit epi-limit, uniform boundary-face lower bound, or exact-minimizer recovery theorem under a hard discordance budget.
proposed.consumer: A solution would turn first-order-equivalent design laws into a path-specific exact-minimax tie-breaker and would determine the accumulation set of exact finite minimizers.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed question directly uses the corrected profile handle and the mixed-coordinate functional, so its claim and free-symbol metadata must be replaced atomically while its established dependencies are preserved.

proposed.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.

For the unrestricted bounded-interval class, independent assignment and a nonlinear rule attain the all-estimator minimax value; the endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the lower side needed to transfer that value and procedure to the present binary endpoint subclass.

Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.

Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove a matching second-order lower expansion and an epi- or \(\Gamma\)-convergence theorem for the finite design-profile risks, identify the resulting contact set in each of the finite-\(\kappa\), \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) regimes, and prove that precisely those contacts are limits of exact finite minimizers.
open_obligations.obstruction: Theorem 5 controls risk only up to \(o(J^{-1})\), whereas selection on the proposed scale requires uniform \(J^{-4/3}\) expansions over interior and boundary schedule faces. The exact finite certificates determine each fixed grid but provide neither a limiting local kernel nor the liminf, equicoercivity, convergence-of-minima, and exact-recovery statements needed to pass finite argmin sets to a measure-valued contact set.
open_obligations.attempted: The finite orbit contact systems, the scalar and two-parameter shrinking-prior lower experiments, and the balanced-orbit centered-estimator upper bound yield the exact first-order face. Expanding the known first-order information game is flat on that face. The hard-budget correction identifies the critical scale algebraically and separates the one-sided candidate domains, but no available calculation supplies its matching lower expansion or the pair-orbit analogue of the unrestricted Airy functional uniformly on all boundary faces.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact finite contact system in Theorem 1 computes every set \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\), and Theorem 5 gives the rigorous first-order statements
\[
 \mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\subseteq\mathcal F_\rho
\]
and recovery of every \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\) by invariant procedures whose excess worst risk is \(o(J^{-1})\). These conclusions do not replace those procedures by exact minimizers.

The critical scale follows algebraically from the candidate hard-budget correction. Indeed, with \(\overline m_J=\int m\,d\mu_{q_J}\),
\[
 J^{4/3}
 \frac{(2\overline m_J-1)\Delta_J}{J^2}
 =\frac{\Delta_J}{J^{2/3}}(2\overline m_J-1)
 =\kappa_J(2\overline m_J-1).
\]
Thus it competes with a \(J^{-4/3}\) unrestricted Airy correction exactly when \(\Delta_J=O(J^{2/3})\). On \(\mathcal F_{1/2}\), \(1/2\le\int m\,d\mu\le1\). Consequently the candidate hard-budget term with \(\kappa_J\to+\infty\) is finite only on \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\). If \(\kappa_J\to-\infty\), subtracting \(\Delta_J/J^2\) changes that term to
\[
 2\kappa_J\left(\int m\,d\mu-1\right),
\]
which is nonnegative and diverges off \(\int m\,d\mu=1\). For \(\rho>1/2\), the first-order face already imposes \(\int m\,d\mu=1/2\); selection then depends on transverse finite-grid deviations and requires a separate tangent expansion. These are consequences of the candidate upper correction and identify the residual regimes, not a proved epi-limit.

prose_updates.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-selected sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction yields an exact finite conic game, a polynomial-size rational kernel, and dual certificates for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; an exact \(J=2,s=1\) certificate rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while the leading term is flat on a measure-valued face at and above the threshold. The unresolved selection problem is now localized at \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\): the candidate hard-budget correction competes with the unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) Airy scale, but only an upper construction is presently available. At \(s=J\), the class is exactly the unrestricted binary class, while comparison with the larger bounded-interval class transfers the same value and procedure only by a two-sided sandwich.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax results cover unrestricted binary schedules, a larger unrestricted bounded-interval class, superpopulation matched-pair precision under half-treatment constraints, or linear shrinkage under a fixed stratified design. They do not solve the intermediate fixed-population class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap while jointly choosing every assignment law and every measurable estimator, and they do not characterize limits of exact finite minimizers on the flat first-order face. The superpopulation half-treatment and fixed-design linear-estimator comparators are non-nested with the present problem.
project_justification.niche: The latent discordance restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without pretending that unobserved potential-outcome similarity is pretreatment information. It creates a finite nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean rules can be jointly optimal, with a critical hard-budget perturbation at \(s_J-J/2=O(J^{2/3})\).
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the normalized orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk frontier, the sharp first-order phase transition, its first-order design face, and exact randomization-test inversion. It additionally formulates, but does not solve, the residual \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled epi-limit and exact-minimizer contact problem.

prose_updates.related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies a symmetry template, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design may require randomization over several partitions; neither solves the present all-estimator hard-discordance game. SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 treats exactly the unrestricted binary class obtained here at \(s=J\), including Bernoulli assignment, a nonlinear posterior-mean rule, and an Airy second-order expansion. Hull2026BoundedOutcomes treats a larger bounded-interval class. The present binary endpoint is only its endpoint-valued subclass: Hull's uniform procedure bounds the binary minimax value from above, while Hull's endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the reverse lower bound, so the same value and procedure transfer without class identity or experiment equivalence. Bai2022MatchedPairs studies a superpopulation stratified problem constrained to treat half of each stratum; deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage studies a fixed-design problem optimized only over linear combinations of group estimators. Those two problems are different from and non-nested with the present fixed-population joint design--all-estimator game. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 and AronowLopatto2026 inform assignment dependence under specified estimator or unbiasedness restrictions. Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion, but their product or fixed-stratum mechanisms do not cover correlated noncanonical laws under a latent mismatch sensitivity class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected kernel has been checked by exact row normalization for every \((h,n)\) at \(J=2,3,4\), and exact rational inequalities certify the strict noncanonical separation only at \(J=2,s=1\). Other displayed finite risks and projected face diagnostics are numerical early-kill checks, not theorem contributions; in particular, the critical grids \(J=2,s=1\) and \(J=4,s=2\) do not establish a stable exact-selection law. The first-order van Trees arguments use smooth boundary-vanishing priors on finite positive-cell experiments and positive finite-\(J\) information regularization, but they control only the \(J^{-1}\) term. Writing \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\) shows that the candidate design correction \((2\overline m_J-1)\Delta_J/J^2\) meets an unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) Airy correction on the \(J^{2/3}\) budget scale. This correction is upper-bound evidence only. No matching lower expansion, boundary-uniform pair-orbit local experiment, epi-limit, convergence of minima, or exact-minimizer recovery theorem has been proved; finite \(\kappa\), the two infinite one-sided regimes, and fixed \(\rho>1/2\) must be analyzed separately.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not an observed or administratively verifiable quantity. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence. The finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. At \(s=J\), the schedule class is exactly the unrestricted binary class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026. It is only the endpoint-valued subclass of Hull2026BoundedOutcomes' bounded-interval class; equality of minimax values and transfer of the Bernoulli nonlinear procedure follow by the uniform-upper-bound and endpoint-prior lower-bound sandwich, not by class identity. For \(\rho\ge1/2\), exact finite minimizers may select a strict subset of the first-order face. The \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled candidate with hard-budget term \(\kappa(2\int m\,d\mu-1)\) is not yet a proved limit, and the exact contact set remains open in the finite-\(\kappa\), one-sided infinite-\(\kappa\), and fixed-supercritical regimes.

statement_notes.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face; the corrected question identifies the \(J^{2/3}\) critical budget scale on which that selection can first interact with the unrestricted \(J^{-4/3}\) correction.
statement_notes.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 supplies an unrestricted scalar Airy expansion, but no published result supplies the measure-valued pair-orbit epi-limit, the boundary-uniform hard-budget lower expansion, or exact-minimizer recovery required here.
statement_notes.consumer: The answer would identify which first-order-equivalent assignment laws are limits of exact finite minimax choices along each sensitivity path and would provide the design analyst's smaller-order tie-breaker.

proofs.proof_tex:
Throughout, the potential-outcome schedule is fixed and the only expectation is over the assignment law, as required by \(\texttt{ass:design-exogeneity}\) and \(\texttt{def:randomization-risk}\).

First let \(0\le s\le s'\le J\).  If \(Y\in\Theta_{J,s}\), then \(D_a(Y)\le s\le s'\) for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Hence, directly from \(\texttt{def:bounded-mismatch-class}\),
\[
 \Theta_{J,s}\subseteq\Theta_{J,s'}.
\]
The condition in \(\texttt{def:design-class}\) restricts a law only to be selected ex ante and independently of \(Y\); the numerical sensitivity label may inform which law is selected but does not remove any outcome-independent assignment law from the feasible simplex.  Thus \(\mathfrak Q_{J,s}=\mathfrak Q_{J,s'}\), while \(\mathfrak D_J\) is the same set at both sensitivity values by \(\texttt{def:estimator-class}\).  Consequently, for every feasible \((Q,\delta)\),
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\Theta_{J,s}}\mathcal R_{J,s}(Q,\delta;Y)
 \le
 \sup_{Y\in\Theta_{J,s'}}\mathcal R_{J,s'}(Q,\delta;Y),
\]
where the two risk formulas agree pointwise by \(\texttt{def:randomization-risk}\).  Taking the infimum over the common feasible procedure class and applying \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\) gives
\[
 R^*(J,s)\le R^*(J,s').
\]

Now set \(s=0\).  By \(\texttt{def:bounded-mismatch-class}\), every \(Y\in\Theta_{J,0}\) has constants \(y_j(0),y_j(1)\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 Y_{j1}(a)=Y_{j2}(a)=y_j(a),
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\},\quad 1\le j\le J.
\]
Under \(q^{\mathrm{pair}}\), exactly one member of each pair is treated.  Define the measurable estimator
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{pair}}(A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J\sum_{r=1}^2
 \bigl\{A_{jr}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}-(1-A_{jr})Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}\bigr\}.
\]
Each pair contributes a number in \([-1,1]\), so \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{pair}}\in[-1,1]\) and therefore belongs to \(\mathfrak D_J\).  Pair homogeneity and consistency in the definition of \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\) imply, assignment by assignment,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{pair}}
 =\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J\{y_j(1)-y_j(0)\}
 =\frac1{2J}\sum_{j=1}^J\sum_{r=1}^2
 \{Y_{jr}(1)-Y_{jr}(0)\}
 =\tau(Y),
\]
the last equality being \(\texttt{def:sate}\).  Thus the worst-case randomization risk of this procedure is zero.  Squared loss is nonnegative, so \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\) yields
\[
 R^*(J,0)=0.
\]

It remains to show that the optimal invariant orbit law is unique at this endpoint.  Let \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\) place positive mass on some \(n\ne(0,0,J)\).  Then every assignment in orbit \(n\) contains an unmixed pair.  Choose one labelled assignment \(a\) in that orbit and one such pair \(j\).  By the orbit construction, \(Q(a)=q_n/C_n>0\).  Let \(Y^{(0)}\) be the all-zero schedule.  If pair \(j\) is all control under \(a\), obtain \(Y^{(1)}\) by setting \(Y^{(1)}_{j1}(1)=Y^{(1)}_{j2}(1)=1\) and leaving all other potential outcomes zero.  If pair \(j\) is all treated, instead set \(Y^{(1)}_{j1}(0)=Y^{(1)}_{j2}(0)=1\).  In either case, both schedules lie in \(\Theta_{J,0}\), and they produce the same observed data under \(a\).  Their SATEs are respectively zero and \(\varepsilon/J\), where \(\varepsilon=1\) in the all-control case and \(\varepsilon=-1\) in the all-treated case.  Therefore, if \(d\) is the common estimator value at that observed-data cell,
\[
 \max\left\{d^2,\left(d-\frac{\varepsilon}{J}\right)^2\right\}
 \ge \frac1{4J^2}.
\]
For at least one of \(Y^{(0)}\) and \(Y^{(1)}\), nonnegativity of all the other assignment contributions then gives
\[
 \mathcal R_{J,0}(Q,\delta;Y)
 \ge \frac{q_n}{4C_nJ^2}>0.
\]
Thus no such \(q\) can attain the already established value zero.  The only remaining orbit law is \(\delta_{(0,0,J)}=q^{\mathrm{pair}}\), so \(\texttt{def:finite-optimal-design-set}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal Q^*(J,0)=\{q^{\mathrm{pair}}\}.
\]

Finally set \(s=J\).  Every binary schedule has \(D_a(Y)\le J\), and hence
\[
 \Theta_{J,J}=\{0,1\}^{\mathcal P_J\times\{0,1\}}
\]
by \(\texttt{def:bounded-mismatch-class}\).  This is exactly the unrestricted binary fixed-population class studied by \(\cite{SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026}\).  Since the design, estimator, target, and loss in \(\texttt{def:unrestricted-endpoint-risk}\) are the same as those in \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\) at \(s=J\), their defining infimum--supremum problems coincide, and therefore
\[
 R^*(J,J)=r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}.
\]

For clarity, this binary-class identity is distinct from the comparison with \(\cite{Hull2026BoundedOutcomes}\).  Let
\[
 \mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}=\{0,1\}^{\mathcal P_J\times\{0,1\}},
 \qquad
 \mathcal Y_{[0,1]}=[0,1]^{\mathcal P_J\times\{0,1\}},
\]
and let \(V_{[0,1]}\) denote Hull's minimax value on \(\mathcal Y_{[0,1]}\).  Then \(\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}\subsetneq\mathcal Y_{[0,1]}\): the former is only the endpoint-valued subclass of the latter.  By \(\texttt{lem:unrestricted-binary-bernoulli-minimax}\), Hull's independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) design and nonlinear posterior-mean rule, denoted \((Q_H,\delta_H)\), obey the uniform bounded-interval upper bound
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{[0,1]}}
 \mathcal R(Q_H,\delta_H;Y)=V_{[0,1]}.
\]
Restriction of this one procedure to binary observations is feasible for the binary problem, so
\[
 r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}
 \le \sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}}
 \mathcal R(Q_H,\delta_H;Y)
 \le V_{[0,1]}.
\]
The same cited lemma supplies a least-favourable prior \(\Pi_H\) supported on endpoint schedules, hence supported on \(\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}\), whose optimal Bayes risk is \(V_{[0,1]}\).  For every binary procedure \((Q,\delta)\), the supremum dominates its \(\Pi_H\)-average risk.  Taking infima gives the reverse inequality
\[
 r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}
 =\inf_{Q,\delta}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}}
 \mathcal R(Q,\delta;Y)
 \ge
 \inf_{Q,\delta}\int_{\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{bin}}}
 \mathcal R(Q,\delta;Y)\,d\Pi_H(Y)
 =V_{[0,1]}.
\]
Thus the two values are equal and \((Q_H,\delta_H)\), restricted to binary data, attains \(r^{\mathrm U}_{2J}\).  This is a uniform-upper-bound plus endpoint-prior-lower-bound sandwich; it does not identify the binary and bounded-interval parameter classes or their experiments.

Under independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment, every labelled assignment has probability \(4^{-J}\).  Orbit \(n\) contains \(C_n\) assignments, so its mass is
\[
 Q_H\{A\text{ lies in orbit }n\}=\frac{C_n}{4^J}=q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}
\]
by \(\texttt{def:canonical-segment}\).  The binary schedule class and squared-error loss are invariant under \(G_J\); averaging the optimal procedure over this finite group leaves the already invariant Bernoulli design unchanged and, by convexity of squared loss, cannot increase its maximum risk.  The lossless invariant reduction in \(\texttt{thm:orbit-game-face}\) therefore supplies an invariant orbit estimator \(\eta\) achieving \(R^*(J,J)\) with orbit law \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\).  By \(\texttt{def:finite-optimal-design-set}\),
\[
 q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\in\mathcal Q^*(J,J),
\]
and the unrestricted attaining procedure is the asserted nonlinear posterior-mean rule.
